name: Aegeline

lead: Aegeline is a compound found in the leaves of the bael tree (Aegle marmelos). Preclinical studies reported anti-hyperlipidemic and glucose-related effects, and from around 2012 it was added to weight-loss and muscle-building supplements marketed for fat loss and a leaner physique.

Its appearance connection was the fat-burner market: users took such products hoping for reduced body fat. After a 2013 cluster of liver injuries in Hawaii among people who had used OxyELITE Pro, aegeline became one of the ingredients investigated by health authorities, and no published human trial of aegeline for fat loss exists.

paras: Aegeline appeared as one ingredient in multi-ingredient oral fat-burner products rather than as a stand-alone item. This article gives no dosing guidance.

The CDC and Hawaii health department reported acute hepatitis cases, with hospitalizations, liver transplants and a death, among people who had used OxyELITE Pro. Investigators said they could not determine which ingredient was responsible, and some researchers have suggested aegeline. The FDA said it was a new dietary ingredient without required notification.

chain: Intended to support fat loss or metabolic effects
angle.text: Aegeline was marketed inside weight-loss supplements to help users get leaner. Animal and cell studies point to metabolic mechanisms, but no human trial has shown fat loss from it.

lead: Aegeline is a compound isolated from the leaves of the bael tree, Aegle marmelos, which has been studied in animals for anti-lipid, anti-diabetic and anti-inflammatory activity [1][2]. In recent years it was added to several weight-loss products, including OxyELITE Pro and VERSA-1 [3].

Its role in looks is through the fat-loss supplement category: people take thermogenic or fat-burner supplements to reduce body fat and look leaner. Published research on aegeline itself is preclinical, including a pharmacokinetic study in mice and work on synthetic analogues acting on the beta-3 adrenergic receptor [3][4].

In 2013 the Hawaii Department of Health and the CDC investigated a cluster of acute hepatitis cases, most in people who had used OxyELITE Pro; a later analysis noted that the product's DMAA-free formulas contained aegeline, which the FDA considered a new dietary ingredient [5][6].

paras: Aegeline was added to weight-loss supplements, including OxyELITE Pro, for users seeking fat reduction [3]. Its reported effects in preclinical models include lipid-lowering and insulin-related activity [1][4].

In the Hawaii investigation 29 cases of acute hepatitis met the case definition; 24 used OxyELITE Pro in the preceding 60 days, 11 were hospitalized, two received liver transplants and one died [5]. A further analysis of 44 cases reported 36 with OxyELITE Pro use, noted that cases followed the introduction of the DMAA-free aegeline-containing formulas, and said whether aegeline or another ingredient was responsible was not yet known [6].

Both reports stress that attributing injury to a single ingredient is difficult, since the products contained several ingredients, product testing did not identify a known hepatotoxin, and observational data cannot prove causation [5][6]. A mouse pharmacokinetic paper describes the supplement-liver-failure link as reported in humans [3].

Aegeline was predicted by structure-activity modelling to be a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist, and synthetic mimics were later tested for insulin sensitivity [4]. In mice, it is absorbed rapidly with a half-life of about 1.3-1.4 hours [3].

US dietary-supplement regulation requires safety information for ingredients not marketed before 1994, and recent amendments mandate adverse-event reporting [7]. The FDA considered aegeline a new dietary ingredient in the OxyELITE Pro context [6].
No studies found. Published work on aegeline consists of animal and cell research [1][3][4], plus epidemiological investigations of supplement-associated liver injury [5][6].

timeline.event: Hawaii Department of Health and CDC investigate acute hepatitis cases linked to OxyELITE Pro [5].
FDA states that aegeline in the DMAA-free formulas is a new dietary ingredient [6].
